blocks.text: May it please you, my Lord, first of all we're grateful to the court for the additional time this morning. Thank you.

blocks.text: There are two matters that we wish to raise with your Lordship. We could either do that straightaway now or we can deal with it after the evidence has been called this morning if the court wishes to press straight on. Neither of them require any decision imminently, just whatever is more convenient for your Lordship. They're relatively brief matters and I've informed your Lordship of them.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, I've seen what they are. Obviously you have seen them as well, Mr Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Perhaps we can deal with them later today rather than keeping the jury waiting.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That's what I thought.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: As far as today is concerned, I understand -- obviously I received a communication about witnesses.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Is it going to be a relatively normal day?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We don't believe so, my Lord. We think we'll be through the evidence before the normal close of business. Quite how quickly is difficult to be sure about, but our instinct is that we're going to come up a bit short, I'm afraid.

She's been told that if at any point she is not able to continue, she should indicate by raising a hand and I will confirm that. But it might be some measure of reassurance to her. She says she's perfectly fit to continue apart from the embarrassment of the injury. So I'm just mentioning it.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. Just to reassure the court, we are looking ahead, both to the immediate, medium and long-term and doing our best to choreograph things to minimise the amount of time during a normal court day that we can't occupy, but from time to time, because of the fairly unusual circumstances of all the witnesses in this case, I'm afraid we simply can't...
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I know it's very difficult and I've mentioned it more than once to the jury and they understand, I am sure, the difficulties. The actual conduct of a trial requires an awful lot of things and people to come together at exactly the same time.

blocks.text: Yes. We did contemplate dealing with the [Baby F] sequence of events, but the chronology there is so important.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, no, it'll create much more confusion and difficulty. It's better to keep things in relation to each individual child. Thank you very much indeed.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Jury, please.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: May I hand up a paginated bundle of statements to be read during the course of today?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (Handed)
(In the presence of the jury)

Good morning, members of the jury. I'm sorry we're a bit delayed starting. I don't know whether you had any travel difficulties starting, but there have been travel difficulties and that's why we're a bit late starting.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I know that one of you had a misfortune overnight and had a fall. You've been told, if at any point you want to break, please just indicate, would you? I have been told by counsel, that's added another couple of minutes' delay in me finding out what the programme for today is, that it's probably not going to be a completely full day in any event, but if at any time you want a break or anything, please just indicate. If you raise a hand we'll see you and we'll just have a break. All right? Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Mr Driver.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Due to some logistical challenges, we're not going to be able to present the evidence in strictly chronological order today. But in an effort to maintain some sense of chronology, before calling the next witness may I read the relevant parts of a statement of a midwife by the name of Susan Brooks.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That's at page 1 of the reading bundle.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: This was a name that was mentioned yesterday, Susan, the midwife.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That's her.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Right. You'll remember this is agreed evidence that's being read to you. As far as these logistical difficulties being referred to, I don't like there being mysteries if they can be avoided. It's just that some witnesses who were scheduled to be here today -- is it more than one witness?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: One that was scheduled cannot be here and the witness we would have like to have called first is stuck in traffic.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Such are the difficulties. Nothing for you to speculate about because if there are mysteries, people tend to speculate about mysteries. That's the reason. So what Mr Driver is going to do is to read these statements. Listen carefully and remember it's evidence in the case just as much as if the witness were here giving the evidence.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Witness statement of SUSAN BROOKS (read)

I wonder if I can invite Mr Murphy to put on screen the nursing notes that Mr Astbury sent him earlier this morning during the course of the reading of this statement, because the maker of this statement is the author of those notes.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Her statement is dated 2 April 2019. It reads as follows:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I qualified from Chester University in 2008 as a registered midwife with a diploma in midwifery. Prior to this date I had been a student between 2005 and 2008 at Chester, and I have worked there since this time.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "In 2015 I was on my rotation to the antenatal and post-natal ward, which is ward 32, and at this point I was a band 6 midwife. I have been asked to provide an account detailing my involvement on 3 August 2015 with a patient named [Mother of Babies E & F].
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Prior to my interview, I have accessed the relevant medical records for this patient. These notes have assisted with my recollection of events during that time.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "There would have been two midwives working the night shift, which commenced on 3 August 2015, and I would have been the shift leader. I would have started my shift at 20.00 hours and this would have ended at 8.30 hours the following morning. [Mother of Babies E & F] was one of the patients I was allocated to look after during this night shift.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "My responsibilities in my working role include ensuring that the patients are post-natally well, both physically and providing any emotional support that is needed.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "On 3 August 2015, in my patient care notes, I have written..."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: And I'm now going to read from her statement which reflects the contents of those patient care notes that you can see on screen, members of the jury.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: So the notes read:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Care since 2000 hours. [Mother of Babies E & F] was postnatally well. I had given her some medication and she asked me to let her know if there was any contact overnight from neonatal unit as one of the twins had deteriorated slightly at that time.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Then at 23.30, I have recorded in my notes that I had a call from the neonatal unit to ask if [Mother of Babies E & F] could go down in 30 minutes as [Baby E] had a bleed and required intubating and that he was very poorly.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "At 23.50 I have recorded that [Mother of Babies E & F] was obviously very distressed and wanted to go to the NNU straightaway. So I asked Stephanie to ring to see if that was okay whilst I continued providing support to [Mother of Babies E & F]."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Just pausing there, that Stephanie was a midwife colleague.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: That part hasn't been read from the statement, but just so you know who Stephanie is.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm grateful, my Lord:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "[She] asked her colleague Stephanie to ring to see if it was okay for [Mother of Babies E & F] to go down immediately whilst I continued providing support to [Mother of Babies E & F]. I felt that she needed to go down straightaway and be with her baby. She was crying and was desperately upset. I thought this 30-minute wait was unreasonable and I made the decision to take [Mother of Babies E & F] to the NNU as it didn't sit comfortably with me.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I have recorded that at midnight I took [Mother of Babies E & F] down to the neonatal unit and I do remember doing this and that her husband, [Father of Babies E & F], was on his way to the hospital. I think that I spoke to [Father of Babies E & F] during a phone call as [Mother of Babies E & F] was so upset, but I can't recall any more detail in relation to the content of that call.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "The neonatal unit is only a five-minute walk from the labour unit and presumably [Mother of Babies E & F] and I would have taken the lift and I would have used my pass to gain access to the NNU. When we arrived at the neonatal unit, they made us wait
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: in the corridor and [Mother of Babies E & F] sat on a chair opposite nursery 1 where the twins were.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "A female nurse approached us and told us we had to wait and I just remember trying to get [Mother of Babies E & F] through those minutes before she was allowed to see [Baby E]. After spending around 10 minutes with [Mother of Babies E & F], she was allowed into the nursery and I handed over her care to my NNU colleagues. I then returned to the labour ward where I continued to care for my other patients.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I have been read a small extract from a statement provided by [Mother of Babies E & F], whereby [Mother of Babies E & F] describes being upset following her visit to the NNU and her telling me what had happened when she returned to my ward. I cannot recall any specific conversation taking place and I have not been provided with any details by [the relevant police officer] as to any event which took place while [Mother of Babies E & F] was in the NNU.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "My only reference to this entry is in my notes documented at 20.00 hours when [Mother of Babies E & F] has asked to be notified of any contact overnight from the NNU due to the deterioration of one of the twins."
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: That concludes the relevant parts of that midwife's notes and statement.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: My Lord, may I call Dr Christopher Wood to give evidence, please.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: DR CHRISTOPHER WOOD (affirmed)
Examination-in-chief by MR DRIVER
Could you state your full name, please?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Dr Christopher Mark Wood.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. May Dr Wood sit down to give evidence?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, certainly.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Dr Wood, could you tell us in general terms the nature of your current profession?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. I'm a general practitioner on the Wirral.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. We understand, and could you confirm, that as of 2015, in the summer of 2015, you were on a trainee placement at the Countess of Chester Hospital? Is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: And for how long were you training at that hospital?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Four months.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: And what sort of training were you undertaking?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I was in my second year of my general practitioner training.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Where within the Countess of Chester were you placed?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It was a split between the paediatrics and neonates units.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: And can you remember the months of the year that you were at Chester?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Between April and ending on 5 August, I believe.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. Your time between those two units, was it shared equally or was it not possible to analyse it in that way?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It was roughly equal. Probably a little bit more paediatrics.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: You have previously made a witness statement in relation to events concerning twins by the [surname of Babies E & F].
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: And could you confirm that prior to making that witness statement, you were afforded and took the opportunity to remind yourself of entries in the clinical notes pertaining to those two twin boys?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Is it right that you were present at their birth --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: -- as part of the medical team in attendance at what was a caesarean section delivery?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: And was your contribution in that regard focused primarily on the twin boy [Baby F]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: After assisting as called upon at and immediately after the delivery, did you have little or nothing to do with the twins for a few days?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: But can you confirm that you were on duty on the 3rd going into 4 August 2015?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I can.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: And what were you doing primarily on that evening of 3 August?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I was the on-call SHO, the more junior of the two doctors on the units. I will have been primarily on the paediatric unit. It was an area I felt more comfortable with with my background training, but will have been called to the neonates unit should the need arise.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. You intimated that you were the more junior of the two doctors on duty that night. Can you recall who your immediately senior colleague was that evening?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I understand it was Dr Harkness, the registrar.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: And was Dr Harkness somebody who you'd worked with previously during the course of your trainee placement at Chester?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: I will invite Mr Murphy to put the carousel on to the screen, please. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Could we go, please, to tile 150?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Before we look at any clinical notes or any records to which you may have contributed, Dr Wood, do you recall when approximately and in what circumstances you first involved yourself with the baby [Baby E] during this shift that you've been describing to us?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: My apologies, I can't remember the exact time. It was in the early hours or potentially just before midnight.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: But the general circumstances?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I understand from the medical records, it was a crash call, so an emergency call to the neonates unit.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: So a crash call for you to attend to the neonates unit.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: From memory, where were you when you received that call?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I believe I was in the doctors' room on the paediatrics unit. I was writing up notes from the previous case I'd just seen.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: And that case was a patient on the paediatrics unit or the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It will have probably been the paediatrics unit or it could have been in A&E, where I would also be called to throughout the night.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: From memory, are you able to say whether you'd undertaken any duties on the neonatal unit during that shift prior to you responding to the crash call you have just alluded to?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I don't recall being there.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Is that as in you weren't there or you don't have a working memory?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I believe from reading the notes, I couldn't recognise my handwriting in any of the records I'd seen, but I can't remember, I'm afraid, any more than that.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. You will see on screen, Dr Wood, and I'm going to deal with these entries as per our visual presentation here, that we are now focusing upon events on or around 23.45 hours on Monday, 3 August. You'll see there, there's reference to Dr Harkness making retrospective -- making clinical notes retrospectively about events at around this time.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The next tile, please, Mr Murphy, 151. It bears your name and if we click behind that and we go to the original document beneath. Do you recognise the signature thereon?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I do, that's my signature, yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: It's your signature. And do you recognise the type of document that you've signed there?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It would be a prescription chart for the baby.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Does it inform us what had been prescribed for the baby at this point?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It does. It indicates an infusion of morphine sulphate, mixed with 10% glucose, a sugar solution.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Mr Murphy, if we could go back to the preceding tile, please, or preceding document behind tile 150. Here is a note from Dr Harkness. If we could scroll down there, we can see the words, "Morphine bolus given", and if you read above, Dr Wood, you can see it's in the context of the baby being intubated as an emergency.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: The attempt to pass a size 3 ET tube into the baby, followed by a successful attempt to pass a size 2.5 tube, and the baby being put on a ventilator.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Having looked at that note and the morphine prescription to which you're a signatory, can you give us the context of the introduction of morphine to the baby at this point in time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I don't specifically recall making those notes, but certainly it would usually be in that situation where if a registrar was intubating, I would have very little experience of intubating at that stage in my career, especially a baby. My experience up to that point and beyond is in adult medicine. So the most useful thing I could be doing at that point would be the tasks that don't require his expertise. So in all likelihood, I would imagine I will have been asked to do the prescription as a formality in order to allow him to administer that medication to the baby. I'm not exactly sure on the context, I'm afraid.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Are you able to assist as to the purpose of the use of morphine with a neonate at the point of the introduction of an ET tube or not?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Not with any degree of certainty, I'm afraid.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: I probably will have known at the time, but not now.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: That's understood, thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No need to worry because the jury have heard about it in relation to other babies.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm grateful.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Do you recall, leaving the notes aside, receiving a crash call?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: I do recall receiving a crash call.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: And you recall your response?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I do, yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Was your response to immediately attend --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It was, yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: -- at nursery 1 in the NNU? And what did you find upon arrival?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: From my recollection, I recall getting there as quickly as I could. I recall there being a number of people already around the baby. And I recall that resuscitation attempts had already begun by the time of my arrival. I believe, again being quite junior there, probably the best thing I could do would be to do the other jobs and allow the more experienced members of the team to do the more specialist parts of the resuscitation. So I believe I switched my attention to scribing, to recording the events, to keeping a note of timings of when medication was administered and when various parts of the resuscitation process were underway, which can serve the role of making sure that things aren't missed and things happen expediently.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. I'm sure we recognise that scribing in these circumstances is an important role, but is it one that is typically undertaken by the most junior doctor present at the scene of an emergency?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: In the context of neonates, yes. It may differ in adult medicine.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. Could we go then, please, to Dr Wood's notes, which are behind tile 164. If we scroll to the bottom, I'm sure you recognise your handwriting, do you?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I do.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. If we go to the staff present. There is a list, according to you, of the people present at points during resuscitation.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: [Dr C] being the consultant?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Dr Harkness, the registrar?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Yourself. And the jury will recognise the other names as being nurses from the NNU, whether or not you remember them from this distance of time.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Does that note indicate that everyone there was present upon your arrival or that they were present at some point during the process?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Present at some point.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. Let's scroll back up then to Dr Wood's first entry. Firstly, Dr Wood, your original notes, would they have been made on the document that's been reproduced as a PDF here or would they have been made on whatever was at hand in the heat of the moment?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Whatever was at hand. It may have been notes with other patient information on it, for instance the handover sheet that I have in my pocket.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. Therefore, does it follow that the time 01.35 on 4/8 was the time of the making of these notes that have been reproduced for our benefit?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I believe so, yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Do the timeline there and the body of this document reflect your contemporaneous record of the time of the key events?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. We'll just invite you to assist us if we struggle with your handwriting.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Does this record that at 00.37 CPR and ventilation had commenced?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Did your colleague inform you that at 00.39, through use of the stethoscope, a good air entry could be found, could be heard?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Then have you recorded the times of the introduction of medication used as part of the resuscitative process --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: -- at 39 and 42 minutes past?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: At 00.43, the baby was auscultated again, good air entry, but does that say "weak heart sounds"?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: The second and third introduction of adrenaline in the minutes thereafter. At 50 minutes past, upon listening again, does that say "weak heart sounds"?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It does, yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Help me with the next entry, the second one at 00.50?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It looks to be:
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: "[Zero] negative blood [O negative blood] infused.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: 20ml per kilogram."
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. So that was the introduction of blood to assist the baby?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I believe so, yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. Further noting of the introduction of the fourth dose of adrenaline, second of bicarb, some dextrose at 00.57. Second adrenaline on the hour.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Help with us with the next at 01.01?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "Auscultated, good air entry, heart rate of less than 90 to 100 beats per minute. Chest compressions stopped.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Ventilations continued."
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Mr Murphy, take us down the page, please. Next entry at 01.09?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Help us, please.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "Auscultated, good air entry, heart rate 70 to 80."
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Next?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: 01.10. It looks to be:
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: "[Query] arterial gas taken."
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: And a saline bolus of 10ml per kg.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Assist the jury as to the meaning of "arterial gas taken" in this context, please.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: During a resuscitation attempt, measuring the components within arterial blood sample can give an indication as to how well things are potentially progressing. It can look at the gases, it can look at the acidity levels, for instance, within the blood.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. So blood taken there and analysed subsequently or immediately?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Immediately whilst the rest of the process is ongoing.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: I believe there's an analyser on the unit for that purpose.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Thank you. And then at 01.15, was it noted that the heart rate, sadly, was failing or falling, does it say?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Falling, I believe, yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: Yes. Compressions were recommenced?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: And then at 01.23, it was deemed, was it, that the process was, tragically, futile --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: WOOD

blocks.text: -- and discontinued? Thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Could we go, please, to tile 158, Mr Murphy?

My Lord, it occurred to me, and I'm grateful to Mr Maher for reminding me, that the second of the two matters that I made reference to relates to the position of witnesses who are due to give evidence again and any additional warnings that either the prosecution or the court may need to give to them in light of material that's available and that can be read. Perhaps I can deal with that point first --
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, certainly.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: -- because it would apply to [Nurse B] and a large number of witnesses who are still to give evidence.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: The concern comes from Ms Letby, and we respectfully share it on her behalf, and put it before your Lordship that she understands indirectly that staff at the Countess of Chester Hospital have, perhaps naturally, been following reports and the news feeds that accompany this case in the media.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Irrespective of what her understanding is, the matter having been raised, it seems to us a matter that is one that the court should properly consider. We don't refer so much to the conventional news reports or news stories that one encounters in the media, but the position now is there are a number of outlets, one in particular, that reports the case in very great detail, with a time given and then sometimes almost a line by line report of what is taken. And we're aware also of at least one website on YouTube which provides a verbatim summary, a very detailed one, of what has happened in the court to the extent of even repeating the content of texts that have been read out as they're gone through in the evidence.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: There's an unusual situation in this case, which is that many of the witnesses who give evidence are then going to return to give evidence and the concern, therefore, which we raise is the prospect of them taking an interest in material that goes into some detail, well beyond conventional news reports, and really, therefore, bypassing the warning given by the court not to talk to other witnesses about their evidence, because it's not very difficult to see a great deal of detail of the evidence. And from that, the anxiety is that it may even affect the way a witness gives evidence. I'm not going to make any suggestions at this point as to where that may or may not have happened. We don't say it hasn't happened, but I'm not going to try and float conjecture at this point as to that. But certainly some accounts have changed as they've travelled along. That may be natural, it may be due to any number of reasons.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: What we would be grateful for in the first instance, my Lord, is that the prosecution take steps to warn witnesses who are going to be giving evidence not to read news feeds or listen to any type of audio news feed or summary, verbatim-style summary, of these proceedings. And by news feeds or verbatim summaries, we mean those pieces which seek to present the evidence almost verbatim, or as much of it as they can, rather than news summaries. We appreciate defining exactly what that is may be a little difficult. But it seems to us it's something that should be done.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: In the same way, respectfully, we ask the court to consider adding a warning in that way to the warning that your Lordship has been giving to witnesses not to discuss their evidence with other witnesses, with anyone in fact, when they are due to return to give evidence or indeed when they've finished.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: But it's important that witnesses are focused on this because if, perhaps quite naturally, they turn their attention to very detailed reporting of what has happened, they are simply receiving all the evidence that other witnesses have said, and that has the danger of having an effect upon the evidence they may give, however inadvertently.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: So that's the problem that we identify, my Lord. We don't go beyond what we propose at this point as a proportionate remedy to it. But we are anxious that the witnesses, particularly those who will return to give evidence, are warned not to read news feeds or verbatim summaries or anything posing as a verbatim summary of these proceedings.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: May I just be clear? You want the prosecution to warn witnesses not to read news feeds or listen to audio news feeds or reports of the evidence?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Are you wanting me to do it as well?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. When a witness has finished.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: At the completion of a witness's evidence in relation to one child when we know that witness is coming back?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, yes, much as your Lordship does in any event when they've finished.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I thought that's what you did want, but it wasn't entirely clear.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That's what we would ask for as a matter of caution in the circumstances.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: All right. Mr Johnson?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Well, this is a problem that we foresaw in our submissions in relation to Twitter.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Exactly.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: So it's not coming as a surprise and I have experience of -- this is a method of reporting on cases which has been going at Liverpool Crown Court for quite some years now actually, so it's not a new problem.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I have never heard of the prosecution being invited to intervene with witnesses to warn them off. But then again, as my learned friend has just said, this case is unusual to the extent that we have repeat witnesses coming back again and again and again.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's the feature.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: It is.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: It is a particular aspect of the way that the evidence is being adduced in this case. Perhaps I can short circuit this: whatever the prosecution do or do not do by way of warning to witnesses, I am of the view that each witness who is going to return to give evidence should be given, in addition to the general direction not to conduct any research or communicate with anyone about anything to do with this case, that I should tell them not to follow live news feeds or read news feeds until they have completed all their evidence in its entirety. blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: No, I don't believe that the court can. It's difficult to know what the sanction would be if a witness...
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, it will be no more than the usual sanction that evidence can be adduced which might lead to the inference that they have broken the sanction and then the credibility and reliability of that witness is or may be destroyed in the eyes of the jury.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Mr Myers, anything you wish to add to that?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: No, we're grateful, my Lord. blocks.text: It's right that the prosecution obviously have a duty in relation to the conduct of the case and one of the duties is to ensure that justice is done. In other words, that the trial proceeds fairly. It's no more than obvious common sense that if a witness does change their evidence by reason of having read a report then it is, as I've said, destructive of their credibility. blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm grateful, my Lord, thank you.

blocks.text: It is dated 6 April 2018. She begins by saying:

blocks.text: "I have been asked to comment on baby [Baby E] and in particular his care on 4 August 2015.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I was working a night shift, the 3rd into 4 August 2015, and was shift leader on this shift. As shift leader I would not normally have an allocated baby to care for but if the unit was particularly busy I could find myself allocated a baby to look after.

blocks.text: Lucy Letby was the designated nurse for [Baby E] on this shift.

blocks.text: Witness statement of SHELLEY TOMLINS (read)
The next and final statement to be read was made by Shelley Tomlins, dated 17 August 2018:
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I am making this statement in relation to an ongoing investigation regarding the neonatal unit of the Countess of Chester period 2015 to 2016.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "When I worked there, I was employed as a neonatal nurse and my role was to care for both premature and sick newborn babies on
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: the neonatal unit. I now reside in Australia and still work as a neonatal nurse. This statement relates to a baby called [Baby E] and I have been asked what involvement I had in relation to his care. I have consulted copies of his medical records and notes prior to completing this statement.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "I am aware from the notes that [Baby E] was born on 29 July 2015. He was one of a set of twins and was the first born of the two of them. They were born at 29 weeks' gestation.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "[Baby E] passed away on 4 August 2015 in the early hours of the morning. I cared for [Baby E] after he died on 4 August 2015 for the day shift starting 07.30 hours the same day. I took handover from my colleague Lucy Letby and shortly after I went to the parent accommodation unit to introduce myself properly to his mum and dad.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "As well as providing emotional support to [Baby E]'s parents that day, my role included liaising with the medical team and also the bereavement coordinator about the practicalities surrounding his death. This was mostly about ascertaining whether [Baby E] was to have a post-mortem, getting the required documentation completed, and deciding when his body was to be moved to the hospital mortuary. I also sat down in discussion with mum, dad and consultant [Dr C] to talk about what most likely caused [Baby E]'s deterioration and death.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Throughout the day I kept the parents updated with any new information known about the coroner's verdict for the postmortem and I am aware that a decision was made not to have one carried out for [Baby E]. Myself and [Dr C] were the staff members to inform the parents about this decision.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "As it was my first time caring for a baby that had died, I sought support and advice from colleagues with the practical aspects of the role. I recall there being a large amount of paperwork. In particular I would have discussed the case with the nurse in charge.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "Unfortunately, I cannot recall with certainty the staff members I worked with that day other than Staff Nurse [Nurse B].
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: "In terms of the physical care of [Baby E], my role was to prepare his body for the mortuary in accordance with the hospital protocol. I did not specifically have a bereavement nursing role whilst at the Countess. As part of our role as neonatal nurses, many of us attended a grief/bereavement study day at Liverpool Women's Hospital and it was expected that we would be able to care for a dying or deceased baby and their family sensitively, should the occasion arise."
